Low-level information about a named pipe

Source: R/info.R
info.Rd

Functions to retrieve low-level information about a named pipe.

  • np_config() returns the pipe configuration.

  • np_state() returns the current clients.

  • np_peek() looks at the bytes of a pipe without reading.

  • np_connected() checks if a client or server is connected to the other side of the pipe.

  • np_sd() returns the security descriptor.

Usage

np_config(con)

np_state(con)

np_peek(con, warn = TRUE)

np_connected(con)

np_sd(con)

Arguments

con

[winpipe].

An open winpipe as created by winpipe.

warn

[logical(1)]

Whether to warn if a pipe cannot be peeked from. np_peek() will run without error even if a pipe can technically not be read from because it is not connected to anything. In this case, it signals a warning and returns 0. Set to TRUE if reading from a disconnected pipe is intended.

Value

np_config() returns:

  • is_server and is_client: Whether the pipe is started as a server or client.

  • is_message_type and is_byte_type: Whether the pipe reads data as bytes or messages. Pipes created using winpipe always read bytes.

  • out_buffer_size and in_buffer_size: Size of input and output chunks.

  • max_instances: Maximum allowed instances.

np_state() returns:

  • state: The reading mode of the pipe. Can be either blocking or non-blocking and byte-mode or message-mode. Pipes created using winpipe should always be in blocking byte-mode.

  • current_instances: Number of instances related to a pipe.

  • username: If con is a server, reports the username of the current client, if any. If con is a client, NA.

np_peek() returns the number of bytes available to read from the pipe. If np_peek() cannot read from the pipe, returns the error code as a warning.

np_connected() returns TRUE when con is a server and a client is connected or when con is a client and a server is connected. If the other side is not connected, returns FALSE.

np_sd() returns an object of class winpipe_sd.

Examples

srv <- winpipe("test")
cli <- winpipe("test")

# client has a server, so np_connected() is TRUE
np_connected(cli)
#> [1] TRUE

np_config(srv)
#> $is_server
#> [1] TRUE
#> 
#> $is_client
#> [1] FALSE
#> 
#> $is_message_type
#> [1] FALSE
#> 
#> $is_byte_type
#> [1] TRUE
#> 
#> $out_buffer_size
#> [1] 1048576
#> 
#> $in_buffer_size
#> [1] 1048576
#> 
#> $max_instances
#> [1] 255
#> 
np_state(srv)
#> $state
#> [1] "blocking byte-mode"
#> 
#> $current_instances
#> [1] 1
#> 
#> $username
#> [1] "runneradmin"
#> 

# Peek can track how many bytes are consumed from reading
np_peek(srv)
#> [1] 0
writeLines("hello\nworld", cli)
np_peek(srv)
#> [1] 12
readLines(srv, n = 1)
#> [1] "hello"
np_peek(srv)
#> [1] 6

np_sd(srv)
#> <winpipe_sd>
#> O:BAG:S-1-5-21-3776380004-1005456608-3524014338-513D:(A;;FA;;;BA)(A;;FA;;;SY)(A;;0x1200a9;;;S-1-5-5-0-854813)

close(srv)

# server closed, so client is serverless
np_connected(cli)
#> [1] FALSE

# peeking is still possible, but signals a warning
np_peek(cli)
#> Warning: The pipe has been ended. (error 109)
#> [1] 0

close(cli)
